rows.options: (1) Client WebSocket transport sends a Ping every ~25 s by default: servers answer automatically, and frames on the wire keep an L7 LB open; non-breaking. (2) Server WebSocketDispatcher idle_timeout on by default at DEFAULT_WS_IDLE_TIMEOUT (75 s, ping at 37.5 s): behaviour change, closes unresponsive peers. (3) gRPC: HTTP/2 PINGs are hop-by-hop and do not cross an LB that terminates HTTP/2, and grpc-go GOAWAYs clients that ping more often than 5 min, so only an application heartbeat on the stream works end to end: a wire decision for an ADR. Recommendation: (1) now, a book section on LB idle settings for WebSocket and gRPC, opt-in client gRPC keepalive; (3) via ADR before any gRPC default changes.

new_findings.finding: The push SSRF pre-flight always resolves the webhook host in this process (tokio lookup_host) and fails the delivery when it cannot, even when HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY will carry the request and the proxy does the resolution. The only way past it, allow_private_urls(), turns the whole SSRF screen off.
new_findings.scenario: Locked-down egress: a pod's resolver answers only cluster names and every external request goes through a corporate proxy that resolves names itself (common with Squid/Zscaler). Every webhook to a public https:// host fails with 'webhook URL hostname could not be resolved', although the proxy path works. book push-notifications/delivery.md discusses the proxy resolving, not this.

new_findings.where: crates/a2a-protocol-client/src/proxy.rs:74-99 and tls.rs:57-69; crates/a2a-protocol-server/src/net/proxy.rs:105-129 and net/client.rs:72-81; hyper-util-0.1.21 client/proxy/matcher.rs:122-133
new_findings.finding: Loopback is never exempt from the proxy variables: hyper-util's Matcher consults only NO_PROXY, and Go's net/http exempts localhost and loopback while this code does not. The SDK allows plaintext http:// only to loopback on the premise that it never leaves the host: the token endpoint (token_provider.rs:790-800, whose error text says so), fetch_jwks (jwks.rs:122-141), server JWKS/OIDC (jwt.rs:1290-1306) and credentialed A2A calls (loopback.rs). With HTTP_PROXY set and no NO_PROXY for localhost, those requests go as forward-proxy requests, in cleartext with their Authorization header or client-secret form, to the proxy host. The client test proxy_and_cert_env.rs:132-160 relies on https://localhost being tunnelled through the proxy.
new_findings.scenario: A pod-wide HTTP_PROXY=http://corp-proxy:3128 (set for all tools), with a sidecar token broker or IdP at http://127.0.0.1:8080: OAuth2ClientCredentials sends 'POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/token' with 'Authorization: Basic <client secret>' across the network to corp-proxy, which then fetches from its own loopback (fails, or reaches the wrong service). A local agent at http://localhost:9000 called with a bearer token leaks it the same way. Probe: `nc -l 3128` as HTTP_PROXY, OAuth2ClientCredentials::new("http://127.0.0.1:9/token", id, secret) -> nc prints the request with the secret.

new_findings.finding: Without the server crate's tls-rustls feature (not in its default features; the SDK does turn it on), the push sender and the model client use Client::builder().build_http(): no HTTP_PROXY, no TCP connect timeout, no keepalive, hyper's 90 s idle pool. The N-B-1 and B-30 fixes apply only to TLS builds.
new_findings.scenario: A deployment depending on a2a-protocol-server directly with default features, delivering to http:// webhooks from a network whose only egress is a proxy: every delivery fails; a black-holed receiver holds each attempt for the full request timeout.

new_findings.finding: For an http:// webhook the request URI is rewritten to the pinned IP before it reaches the proxy connector, so NO_PROXY is matched against the IP, not the webhook's name: a NO_PROXY entry naming the host (or its domain) no longer exempts it. https:// webhooks to the same host do match by name.
new_findings.scenario: NO_PROXY=.partner.example because partner hooks must go direct; http://hooks.partner.example/... is sent to the proxy as 'POST http://203.0.113.5/...', which the proxy denies or routes differently, while the https:// webhook to the same host goes direct.

new_findings.finding: The server's trustworthy_url treats any *.localhost name as loopback and allows plaintext JWKS and OIDC discovery to it. glibc and musl send *.localhost subdomains to DNS unless nss-myhostname or systemd-resolved is in use, so the name is not guaranteed to resolve to loopback. The client's fetch_jwks (jwks.rs:140) does not accept *.localhost, so the two crates disagree.
new_findings.scenario: An operator configures from_jwks_url("http://idp.localhost:8080/jwks") in a container whose resolver forwards it upstream. An on-path DNS answer points it at a host serving attacker keys over plaintext, and tokens signed with those keys validate.
